Yes, the cached data is still there and I can summarize it. Your Google connection is not working right now, though.

**Connection status:** The Google token needs to be reconnected. The status reports `invalid_reconnect_required` and "No verified API connection." Google's consent screen is in Testing mode, so refresh tokens expire after about 7 days. To reconnect, run `ghealth auth login` in your terminal. The server will pick up the new credentials. I did not make a live API call, so I can't confirm whether the token would work today.

**Cached Google steps, October 1–3, 2026** (read from local data only):

| Date | Steps |
|---|---|
| Oct 1 | 1,000 |
| Oct 2 | 2,000 |
| Oct 3 | 3,000 |

- Mean and median: 2,000 steps per day
- Range: 1,000 to 3,000
- Coverage: all 3 days have data

**Limitations:**
- There are only 3 days of data, so no trend can be calculated (it needs at least 6 days).
- The figures are cached from before the connection lapsed. Any steps recorded after the last sync are not included, and the local copy may not match what Google currently holds.
- Days with no records are missing, not zero. These three days all have records.
- Dates follow your Google account's time zone, which the server has set to America/New_York.

If you reconnect and sync, the server can refresh this range and add newer days. This summary is for general information and is not medical advice.
